subject: Post-demo: integration technical questions + resilience checklist

Subject: Post-demo: integration technical questions + resilience checklist

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our end and a short tech checklist so your platform team can prioritize next steps. I copied Jordan (platform) and Marissa (AE).

1) SDK & auth
- We recommend starting with our JS/Go SDKs for the integration points you demoed (structured output/tool-calling + embeddings).
- Auth options: API key for sandbox and service-account (JWT) for long-term production. If you need SSO, we can support OAuth2 with scoped tokens (we'll need the redirect URIs).

2) Routing & fallbacks
- Primary: Redwood hosted inference (low latency).
- Fallback: customer-dedicated pool or lower-cost quantized model for large batches. We can wire this with a simple routing policy in the SDK config (region + cost-priority).

3) Structured output / tool calling
- We'll provide a JSON-schema example for tool-calls (actions + params). Recommend server-side validation of the schema and strict timeout for tool execution.

4) Embeddings & reranker plan
- Use batched embedding calls (we expose a batch endpoint). Cache embeddings on your side (LRU) for frequently-seen vectors. Reranker can run on top of sparse candidate retrieval + a lightweight re-rank model; we'll provide a latency / cost estimate once you share expected QPS.

5) Rate limits, retries & idempotency (initial ask)
- Please confirm expected steady-state QPS and burst profile. From the demo you mentioned ~70–120 req/s for search reranks during normal hours with spikes to ~300 during peak. If that's accurate we'll propose a tiered quota.
- For 429s: add a unique request id (X-Request-ID) and implement exponential backoff with jitter. We recommend reading Retry-After header on 429 responses.

Attachments: "redwood-integration-checklist.pdf" (high-level tasks + sandbox request form).

Next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm QPS/burst and a preferred date for a hands-on integration kickoff (sandbox keys + test dataset).
- We: produce a 1–2 page 429/retry snippet and a small SDK code example for idempotent calls.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up with your infra folks.

— Mina

Sarah — great context, thanks. Looping Neha (solutions lead) and Jordan (serving/runtime) to add a few concrete recommendations; answers below. Attaching a short snippet and a small patch that shows retry headers.

Idempotency / retriable semantics
- Rerank: if your reranker call is pure scoring (no state-change on our side), it's safe to replay. For calls that can mutate state (e.g., logging a click that triggers billing/metrics), use an idempotency-token header. We recommend: 
  - For stateless requests: no special token needed; include X-Request-ID for observability.
  - For state-changing requests: include Idempotency-Key: <uuid> and persist the response server-side if your gateway retries.

Request headers we recommend
- X-Request-ID: uuid v4 (required)
- Idempotency-Key: uuid v4 (optional, for writes)
- X-Client-Timestamp: ISO8601 (optional; helpful for debugging skew)
- X-Retry-Count: integer (middleware can write this)

429 / Retry guidance (short form)
- Respect Retry-After header when present.
- Client-side recommended algorithm: exponential backoff with full jitter: base=200ms, cap=10s, attempts=5. Example backoffs: 200ms, ~400–800ms, ~800–1600ms, ... up to cap.
- For gateway-level retries: keep attempts low (2–3) to avoid thundering herd. Use client-side request-id to correlate.

Routing + quotas
- We'll propose a tiered quota: Sandbox (10 qps), Standard (100 qps), Enterprise (300+ qps). We can support burst buffers for short windows. We'll need to provision capacity for reranker throughput separately (higher CPU per request).

Caching & batching to reduce pressure
- Batch embeddings wherever possible (our batch endpoint accepts up to 512 vectors in one call).
- Cache top-k embeddings server-side for fast retrieval; use TTL aligned with your update cadence.

Deliverables from Redwood (ETA 2 business days):
- "429-handling-snippet.txt" (attached) — short code and HTTP-header guidance.
- Small SDK example that shows Idempotency-Key usage for writes and X-Request-ID propagation.
- Sandbox key request form filled once you confirm kickoff time.

I put a quick checklist in the Drive link (see related links). Jordan, can you confirm if serving requires any additional headers for KV cache priming?

— Mina
